title: The watchlist
why: It is the app's root destination and the screen a reader opens by reflex. Its fold decides how many markets they see before scrolling, and its row cadence is the thing that makes a long list readable or exhausting.

masks.reason: Content. Their BTC and ours were quoted seconds apart and neither number says anything about layout. The price cell's box stays compared; the digits inside it do not.
Content, and additionally a declared colour deviation in light theme.
Content: it is a drawing of the last few hours, which differ.
Symbol artwork is licensed per-exchange and is not the same set on both sides.

measurements.note: Every gap is measured against the first, not against its neighbour. Neighbour-to-neighbour hides a half-pixel that accumulates: five rows down a list that is two and a half pixels, and by row forty it is a visible slope. This is the assertion that catches drift rather than averaging it away.
Thickness and left inset both. An inset that starts under the glyph instead of under the words turns a column of marks into a table of cells.
The fold. Ours is 117 dp and is asserted exactly in FoldMetricsTest; this is the same number measured against theirs in pixels.
The move column running off the row at 393 dp is a fault this app has actually shipped. It is measured, not eyeballed.

known_differences.label: INTENTIONAL_ACCESSIBILITY_DEVIATION
known_differences.what: Light theme marketUp #057A66 and marketDown #D01427, against their #089981 and #F23645.
known_differences.why: Theirs measure below 4.5:1 on our light surface. Ours are 4.62:1 and 5.02:1. Dark theme uses their values unchanged.

known_differences.label: INTENTIONAL_BRAND_DIFFERENCE
known_differences.what: The header carries our own wordmark and its stream animation.
known_differences.why: It is the one piece of this screen that is deliberately ours.

known_differences.label: DYNAMIC_CONTENT
known_differences.what: Every price, percentage, sparkline and symbol mark.
